en: NAK 5-86 = NGMPP B 24/34:
*Parikramapadopāyikā-karmaprasaraś ca*, misread as *Parikramapadopāmikāpadmaprasaraś ca*.
% Most likely the first folio of a manuscript of the *Vajrasattvodayā* [= Tōh. 2517] % a rare work of Ānandagarbha! [1v] \siddham namaḥ śrīvajrasattvāya||
Having prostrated again and again before Vajrasattva, the Lord of the World.
Having prostrated to Vajrasattva,
I shall explain the auspicious *Sādhanopāyikā*, which is the arising of Vajrasattva.
In this auspicious [work],

the procedure for propitiating the noble Vajrasattva is compiled for the yogin who has obtained the pledges (*samaya*) and so forth through the ritual of the great tantra, the *Āryatattvasaṃgraha*, within the great maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu.
[labdha˚] \emend, labda˚ \ms;
[˚samayādikasya] \emend, ˚samayādhikasya \ms; [yogina] \corr, yoginaḥ || \ms.

First, having performed the internal bath through conviction in selflessness (*nairātmya*), one should generate an eight-petaled lotus at the throat region by means of the syllable *hrīḥ*, and a white five-pronged vajra on the petal of the tongue-lotus by means of the syllable *hūṃ*; one should then consecrate it with this [mantra]: "O Vajra-tongue! (*vajrajihve*).
Having performed [it],
with the syllable *hrīḥ*,
on the petal.

Having visualized two lunar discs from the two *a* syllables in the two hands, and upon them two five-pronged vajras from the two *hūṃ* syllables, one should perform the destruction of obstacles and so forth with the needle known as the "hand-finger" (*karasākhya*).
There, having emanated oneself as the sun amidst vajra-flames by means of the syllable *hūṃ*, one should utter: "Oṃ, seize, O Vajra-samaya, hūṃ vaṃ! and bind the *krodhaterintirī* [mudrā].
Having placed the vajra-bind (*vajrabandha*) at the soles of the feet, one should cover [the face] with a wrathful mind.
One should cover [it];
the *krodhaterintirī* is said to be [performed] deeply with the vajra of the thumb.

Then, seated upon the half-vajra throne and having formed the *vajra-terintirī* mudrā, one should receive the vajra-garland initiation with the mantra: *Oṃ vajrajvālānalārka hūṃ abhiṣiñca mām*. Regarding the *vajrabandha*: one should hold the two thumbs joined and raised, pressed together above the *vajrabandha* [mudrā]. This is the *vajra-terintirī*.

Having armored [the practitioner] with the two-syllable armor-mantra "Oṃ ṭum," one should utter: "Oṃ vajrajvālānalārka hūṃ. Having placed the left vajra-fist at the heart and brandishing the right vajra-fist, one shall destroy all obstacles.

Uttering *hūṃ* (or *hūṃ ma*) while brandishing [the hand], one should then perform the burning of obstacles and so forth with the Vajra-fire mudrā accompanied by the ritual gesture. Reciting: *oṃ vajrānala daha paca matha bhañja raṇa phaṭ*, [one forms the mudrā as follows]: within the internal vajra-bind, with the fingers having flames in their midst, the thumb-vajra is raised; this is the Vajra-fire Samaya-mudrā.

Thereafter, with the mantra "Vajranetrī, bind all obstacles," one should perform the binding of all obstacles by means of the appropriate mudrā. Having formed the vajra-bind, one should extend both thumbs and hold them level. This is the Vajranetrī mudrā.
Having placed the extended vajra-bond upon the ground, one should perform the lower bond with the mantra: *oṃ vajra dṛḍho me bhava rakṣa sarvaṃ svāhā*.

Having placed [the hands] below, one should perform the upper binding (*ūrdhvabandha*) with the Vajrabhairavanetra mudrā, accompanied by the mantra: *oṃ hulu 2 hūṃ phaṭ*. Having formed two vajra-fists and whirled them like a circle of firebrands (*alātacakravat*), one should hold them above the head with the index fingers in the shape of hooks (*aṅkuśa*). This is the Vajrabhairavanetra mudrā.

Having bound [the gesture] like a whirling firebrand (*alātacakra*), one should again perform the binding right there with Vajrayakṣa together with his mudrā below it, reciting: *oṃ vajrayakṣa hūṃ*. The mudrā of Vajrayakṣa, the fanged one, consists of the vajra-añjali with both thumbs extended and both index fingers (*tarjanī*) bent in the shape of a hook (*aṅkuśa*).
By the yakṣa, the mudrā is "hūṃ";
the two index fingers are extended.

One should bind the eastern direction with the Vajroṣṇīṣa mudrā, accompanied by the mantra *Oṃ druṃ bandham* or *drum*. Forming two vajra-fists, one should join the two little fingers in a chain-lock (*śṛṅkhalabandha*), rotate the two index fingers so that their tips point forward like needles, and place them upon the crown of the head. This is the Vajroṣṇīṣa mudrā.
Thus, [it is said] "drum" in the manuscript (pcorr), or "iti vā drum" in the manuscript (acorr).
Again, one should bind that very [person] with the vajrapāśa: *hūṃ vajrapāśa hrīḥ*. With two vajra-fists, one should form the outer knot. This is the vajrapāśa-mudrā.

Again, with the Vajrapatākā [mudrā], [one binds] the western [direction]. Reciting: *oṃ vajrapatāke pataṅgiri raṭ*. In the vajrabandha, with the thumbs in the sattvaparyaṅka position, the tips [of the index fingers] are made into needles; the two middle fingers are equal and the ends of the ring fingers are spread apart. This is the Vajrapatākā [mudrā].
In the west,
[with] two [hands] that have split open,
[holding] a vajra-banner.
The supreme Vajrakālī: Oṃ hrīḥ vajrakāli raṭ maḍ. The very mudrā of Vajrayakṣa is firmly applied to the mouth of Vajrakālī.

[With the mantra] *vajraśikhare ruṭ maḍ*, one performs the gesture of lifting up a mountain with both *vajramuṣṭi*s; this is [the mudrā] of Vajraśikhara. For the northern [direction], [one uses] *oṃ vajraśikhare* for the southern [direction]. [The mantra is: *oṃ vajraśikhare ruṭ maḍ*. With the two *vajramuṣṭi*s, there is the performance of the gesture of lifting up a mountain. This is [the mudrā] of Vajraśikhara.
Having performed the binding of the mandala with vajra-action, one should provide a perimeter wall. *Oṃ vajrakarma*. Thus it is said.
